title: Feedback Fragment Annotator — Customer threads and proposed patches
summary: Working synthesis of recently surfaced customer threads (May–Jun 2026) distilled into small patches and candidate product initiatives. Focus: reduce time-to-recovery for inference errors, clarify model-selection behavior in mixed-capacity routes, and lower friction for token-cost investigations. This doc intentionally mixes raw excerpts with proposed micro-proposals so engineers and PMs can pick low-effort wins first.
observations: (1) Several customers report intermittent 503s during short bursts; most see automatic retry loops in client-side SDKs which double token counts before they detect failure. (2) Users are confused when 'model variant fallback' silently returns lower-quality outputs; they expect an explicit signal in the response. (3) Platform customers frequently ask for per-call cost attribution (route -> model -> batch) surfaced in SDKs for troubleshooting. (4) Feature requests cluster into: observability, graceful degradation UX, and cost attribution tools. Frequency: 503s and silent fallback are highest frequency for enterprise customers; cost attribution is high frequency among platform/engineering buyers.
prioritized_requests: 1) Explicit fallback flag in streaming/chunked responses (proto: response.metadata.fallback_reason) — frequent ask from Dedicated customers; low infra change, medium API surface. 2) Retry-debounce header in SDKs to prevent client loops (+server hints) — quick fix via SDK patch. 3) Per-request cost breakdown in console and SDK telemetry (route/model/batch) for top 10 routes — scoped pilot. 4) Error-rate heatmap by region + instance-type in Console — useful for SRE and customers; medium effort. 5) 'Explain routing' endpoint for a sample request showing why a request was routed to X variant — useful for audits and enterprise sales demos.
quick_fixes: - SDK: introduce idempotency token propagation and default backoff + jitter (ETA: 1 sprint). - API: include 'fallback_reason' header when routed to lower-tier model (ETA: engineer can add in 2-3 days to runtime). - Console: add 'recent fallback' quick filter in existing per-route table (ETA: 1 week design + 1 sprint dev). - Support playbook: short template to capture retry multiplies and token impact for billing disputes (ETA: immediate).
larger_initiatives: - Cost attribution pilot (Q3): instrument per-request token accounting end-to-end and expose in Console; requires batching-path instrumentation + cost model harmonization. - Routing transparency project: build explainability API + logging for routing decisions; aligns with sales asks for Dedicated/Private. - Resilience SLA uplift: targeted work to reduce 99p tail for short burst 503s by improving autoscale/backpressure heuristics; cross-team project with infra and serving-runtime.
owners_and_estimates: Suggested owners: SDK retry-debounce (owner: Maya Patel, eng-dx, 1 sprint), fallback flag in runtime (owner: Oliver Grant, eng-serving-runtime, 3 days for header + 1 sprint for tests), console filters (owner: Diego Ramos, product-cs, 2 sprints), cost pilot (owner: product-optimize, exploratory 6 weeks), routing explainability (owner: eng-infra + research, exploratory 8–12 weeks).
open_questions: - Should the fallback_reason be machine-readable codes or free-text? (tradeoffs: compactness vs. debuggability) - Do we surface fallback notifications in streaming chunks or only in final envelope to avoid breaking streaming clients? - For cost-attribution pilot, do we prioritize accuracy (higher backend effort) or fast-but-approximate visibility? - Are legal/compliance teams comfortable with exposing routing rationale for private deployments?
raw_voice_excerpts:
Customer A (SaaS, Dedicated): 'During peak ingestion we saw a bunch of 503s. Our app retried automatically and token usage spiked. We had to pause traffic which is bad for UX.'
Customer B (Platform team): 'We want to be able to tell our billing owner which routes are expensive — right now it's a black box of model selection and batching.'
Customer C (Enterprise): 'There was a fallback to a smaller model and the answers were worse. We only noticed because a human complained — we need an obvious signal.'
next_steps: - Circulate to ENG-serving-runtime and SDK leads this week; request feasibility notes by 2026-06-11. - Quick-win sprint: SDK retry-debounce + runtime fallback header to be scoped in next planning meeting. - Kick discovery for cost-attribution pilot: product + infra sync 2026-06-14. - Add support playbook template to shared CS folder and link in customer replies (owner: Diego Ramos).
